title: [cutover prerequisite] Durable cutover generation evidence and its production reader: distribution manifest, import generation, quiesce record digests
description:
FILED BY architect-1270c677 on 2026-08-29 at HEAD aebdb367, as the measured prerequisite that hard-blocks task-b254847909ca4199a70a3a06173f1cd9 (Cutover activation tooling). The epic rails require prerequisite production tasks with the gap measured symbol by symbol rather than a narrowed DoD or a mock-backed journey; this is that row.

WHAT BLOCKS. task-b2548479's daemon `cutover.activate` must write a v2 activation marker recording the CURRENT generation snapshot at activation time. The marker module already exists as that row's WIP (apps/daemon/src/cutover/cutover-activation-marker.ts, untracked) and it CONSUMES the tuple — `:30` declares `readonly distributionManifestSha256: string` and `:109` reads `input.generations.distributionManifestSha256`. It does not produce it. Nothing else does either, so the values could only come from the caller, and caller-supplied current values would FABRICATE BOTH SIDES of the drift comparison the marker exists to make. That is the exact class of fabricated-authority defect these epics exist to remove.

THE GAP, MEASURED SYMBOL BY SYMBOL at HEAD aebdb367, tracked, repo-wide:
- `distributionManifestSha256` — appears ONLY in packages/benchmark/src/activation-binding.ts, activation-binding.test.ts, activation-record.test.ts. All CONSUMER sites; the admission takes it as input. `git grep -ln 'distributionManifest\|distribution-manifest' HEAD -- apps packages tools` returns only control-room live-dispatch.ts (a DEV_PAYLOADS fixture) and daemon http/bootstrap TEST fixtures. NO durable producer.
- `importGenerationSha256` — appears ONLY in those same three packages/benchmark files. NO producer.
- `quiesceRecordSha256` — same three files only. The live legacy quiesce apparatus landed (tests/migration/cutover-live/live-quiesce-*.ts, commit e73e3aa7) but emits NO digest: `git grep -n 'sha256\|digest\|Digest' HEAD -- tests/migration/cutover-live/live-quiesce-evidence.ts` returns EMPTY.
- `backupGenerationDigest` — this ONE is different and must be composed, not rebuilt. It has a rich durable surface already under apps/daemon/src/recovery/ (recovery-inventory-reader.ts, recovery-inventory-record.ts, recovery-incarnation.ts, recovery-succession.ts, recovery-completion-evidence.ts, durable-recovery-inventory-reader.ts and others).

Also measured absent in the daemon: no `CutoverAttemptState` and no `reduceCutover` consumer or writer (`grep -rn 'reduceCutover\|CutoverAttemptState' apps/daemon/src` is EMPTY, untracked-inclusive), and no authoritative-v2 command gate reads ACTIVE or the marker. `reduceCutover` itself IS landed and barrel-reachable (packages/core/src/cutover/cutover-reducer.ts:235, exported at packages/core/src/index.ts:403).

SCOPE. Land durable, digestible evidence for the three producerless generations, and ONE production reader that returns the four-value snapshot from durable state for a given cutover attempt. NOT IN SCOPE: task-b2548479's marker or daemon service (it consumes this), task-b8272ee0's roster registration, task-c4321b6f's GA execution, and the recovery journey's existing backup evidence, which must be COMPOSED rather than duplicated.

THIS ROW MAY ITSELF NEED SPLITTING. Three independent evidence producers plus a reader may exceed the ten-file plan cap; if the planning architect measures that, split by producer and land the reader last. Say which shape was chosen and why.

MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE, learned expensively on this board today: an ABSENCE premise must be probed UNTRACKED-INCLUSIVE. `git grep <rev>` reads the commit and is blind to untracked files by construction — a producer row was filed this morning for work a live worker had already written in the worktree. Probe with `git status --porcelain` or a worktree `grep -r` ALONGSIDE the HEAD grep, and scan non-terminal rows for the deliverable's filenames before building.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK at claim, recorded in a durable moe.add_comment (the completion summary is write-only and persists nowhere). Re-capture `git rev-parse HEAD` and quote it beside every probe, each UNPIPED with its own exit code and a positive control. Re-run the gap measurement BOTH tracked and untracked-inclusive: for each of distributionManifestSha256, importGenerationSha256 and quiesceRecordSha256 confirm there is still no durable producer, using `git grep -n <sym> HEAD -- apps packages tools` AND a worktree `grep -rn <sym> apps packages tools`. If a producer now exists, ADOPT it and report blocked as duplicate rather than building a second one. Also scan non-terminal rows for these symbols before writing any byte.

Each of the three producerless generations has a DURABLE, SERVER-DERIVED digest recorded by production code - the digest is computed from the artifact it names, never supplied or influenced by a caller, and a caller-presented digest is REFUSED with an exact stable reason code at a named layer, both asserted. For the quiesce record specifically, compose the landed live-quiesce apparatus (tests/migration/cutover-live/) as the artifact source rather than inventing a parallel notion of what quiescence means.

backupGenerationDigest is COMPOSED, NOT REBUILT. It is read through the existing durable recovery surface under apps/daemon/src/recovery/ - name in a row comment exactly which reader you compose and why it is the right one. A fourth notion of backup generation that agrees with the recovery lane today will drift from it tomorrow; that is the same third-notion hazard the board has already been burned by on policy refs.

ONE PRODUCTION READER returns the complete four-value snapshot for a given cutover attempt from durable state, and REFUSES deterministically when any of the four is unavailable - naming WHICH fact was missing, with its exact code and refusing layer. Absence must refuse, never default to a zero digest or an empty string: a zero-filled generation would silently compare equal to another zero-filled one and make the drift comparison vacuous.

RAIL 8(B) CONSUMER EDGE: name task-b254847909ca4199a70a3a06173f1cd9 as the consumer and record its id in a row comment. A reader nothing imports satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist. If one durable call site can be landed without reaching into that row's scope, prefer it and say what you did.

Round-trip and tamper proof over a FILE-BACKED store: each recorded generation reads back byte-identical through the reader; a mutated byte refuses with the exact code; an identical re-record adds ZERO duplicate decision and event rows, asserted as counts with denominators. Mutation drills each redden a NAMED arm - substituting a zero digest for the refusal must red the absence arm, and substituting a DIFFERENT default must red the SAME arm, since absence and a defaulted value are different answers.

Gates standalone, foreground and unpiped, each with exit code AND nonzero count line quoted: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exit 0 quoting its `$ tsc` echo, and the focused daemon suite quoting its `Test Files`/`Tests` counts - the root vitest include has NO apps/**, so a bare `pnpm test` runs zero daemon tests and proves nothing here. Repo-wide red path-attributed merge-base versus delivered owned-path delta with foreign failures disclosed verbatim. Every production file under 400 lines; every new `.ts` with its `.js` bridge; explicit-pathspec commit, never `git add -A`.
taskRails: Never accept a caller-supplied generation digest and never default an absent one to zeros or an empty string. The marker exists to detect drift; a caller-supplied or defaulted value fabricates both sides of that comparison and makes the whole mechanism decorative.

Compose the existing surfaces rather than duplicating them: the recovery lane for backupGenerationDigest, and the landed live-quiesce apparatus for the quiesce artifact. Do not introduce a second notion of either. State in a row comment which reader/artifact you composed and why.

An ABSENCE premise must be probed UNTRACKED-INCLUSIVE - `git grep <rev>` reads the commit and cannot see untracked files. Pair every HEAD grep with `git status --porcelain` or a worktree `grep -r`, and scan non-terminal rows for the deliverable's filenames. A duplicate producer row was filed on this board today for exactly this reason.
This row lands the evidence and its reader. It does NOT implement task-b2548479's marker or daemon cutover.activate service, task-b8272ee0's roster registration, or task-c4321b6f's GA execution.

Shared worktree: commit only owned pathspecs, never `git add -A`; preserve foreign WIP including the untracked apps/daemon/src/cutover/ directory, which is task-b2548479's; no push, no PR comment. Mutation drills in a temp copy or with a restore proven in a call SEPARATE from the restore, by SHA256 for untracked paths since `git diff` is blind to them.
Adopt, never duplicate: re-measure every cited line number and symbol at claim time - they move. If a sibling landed the mechanism first, verify and close rather than re-implement.

implementationPlan.description:
VERIFY-OR-BLOCK GATE (read-only; author no bytes). Record every command and verbatim output in a durable moe.add_comment. Quote `git rev-parse HEAD` beside every probe; run each UNPIPED with its own exit code and a positive control. `cmd | head; echo $?` reports head's status, not the command's.

PROBE UNTRACKED-INCLUSIVE (taskRail 3 — `git grep <rev>` reads the commit and CANNOT see untracked files, and a duplicate producer row was already filed on this board for exactly that miss). For each of distributionManifestSha256, importGenerationSha256 and quiesceRecordSha256 run BOTH `git grep -l <sym> HEAD -- apps packages tools tests` and a worktree `grep -rl <sym> apps packages tools tests`, and quote both counts.
MEASURED AT HEAD aebdb367: tracked 3 files each, worktree 5 each. The two extra worktree files are apps/daemon/src/cutover/cutover-activation-marker.{ts,test.ts} — task-b2548479's UNTRACKED WIP, and a CONSUMER, not a producer. The premise holds: consumers only, no durable producer. If a producer now exists, ADOPT and verify rather than re-implementing.

CONFIRM THE FOUR ARTIFACT SOURCES, because this row DIGESTS them and must never rebuild them:
(a) quiesce — `serializeLiveEvidence` is exported at tests/migration/cutover-live/live-quiesce-evidence.ts:209 and emits the canonical two-space JSON record. Confirm the module still emits NO digest of its own (`grep -n "sha256\|digest\|createHash" <that file>` empty). That absence is why this row exists; if it now emits one, compose it instead.
(b) backupGenerationDigest — 43 tracked hits, a rich durable surface. The composition target is apps/daemon/src/recovery/durable-recovery-inventory-reader.ts (:179-180 already validates the digest against a basis) with its contract at durable-recovery-inventory-contract.ts:72/:248 and shape guard at durable-recovery-inventory-shape.ts:102. Name in your comment WHICH reader you compose and WHY (DoD 3).
(c) distribution manifest — the producing lane is tools/packaging/distribution-{build,inventory,startup}.ts. Identify the exact artifact whose bytes the digest names.
(d) import generation — tools/import/durable-import-store.ts and import-commit.ts.

OWNERSHIP: `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/cutover/` shows the whole directory UNTRACKED and belonging to task-b2548479. This row ADDS files there but must never commit that directory as a pathspec — see step 7.

TDD RED FIRST (epic rail 6) — the refusal arms before the happy path, because absence refusing is this row's whole point. Write these before any production byte and quote each red.

In the NEW apps/daemon/src/cutover/cutover-generation-evidence.test.ts:
(1) A CALLER-PRESENTED DIGEST IS REFUSED with an exact stable reason code at a named layer (DoD 2, taskRail 1). Assert code AND layer, never merely that it failed. This is the arm that keeps the marker's drift comparison honest: a caller-supplied digest fabricates BOTH sides of it.
(2) EACH DIGEST IS SERVER-DERIVED FROM ITS ARTIFACT: recompute the expected value in the arm from the artifact bytes and assert equality. Do NOT assert against a literal — a hardcoded expectation is a fixed point that a stubbed-return mutant satisfies.
(3) A MUTATED ARTIFACT BYTE CHANGES THE DIGEST and a recorded-then-tampered record REFUSES with the exact code (DoD 6).
(4) AN IDENTICAL RE-RECORD ADDS ZERO duplicate decision and event rows — assert the COUNTS with denominators, not merely that no error was thrown.

In the NEW apps/daemon/src/cutover/cutover-generation-reader.test.ts:
(5) THE ABSENCE ARM, and it is the load-bearing one (DoD 4): with any ONE of the four facts unavailable, the reader REFUSES and NAMES WHICH FACT was missing, with its exact code and refusing layer. Sweep all four — a roster of four cases, asserted as an exact count, so a silently dropped case cannot pass.
(6) NEVER DEFAULT: assert the refusal carries no digest at all rather than a zero-filled or empty-string one. A zero-filled generation compares EQUAL to another zero-filled one and would make the drift detection silently vacuous — that is why DoD 4 forbids it and why drill D2 substitutes a zero to prove this arm bites.
(7) THE FOUR-VALUE SNAPSHOT reads back byte-identical over a FILE-BACKED store with close-and-reopen (DoD 6) — not an in-memory one, which cannot show a durability defect.

NEW apps/daemon/src/cutover/cutover-generation-evidence.ts (<=250 lines) plus its one-line `.js` bridge `export * from "./cutover-generation-evidence.ts";`. The repo convention is universal under apps/daemon/src and a missing bridge is invisible to tsc and vitest while redding unrelated files at runtime; runtime-entrypoint.test.ts's gate will also flag a module whose tier and bridge disagree.

IT RECORDS THE THREE PRODUCERLESS DIGESTS DURABLY, each computed SERVER-SIDE from the artifact it names:
- quiesceRecordSha256 — over the canonical bytes `serializeLiveEvidence` already produces (live-quiesce-evidence.ts:209). COMPOSE that function; do NOT re-serialize the record here. A second serialization that agrees today drifts tomorrow, and the digest would then name bytes nobody else can reproduce (taskRail 2).
- distributionManifestSha256 — over the distribution manifest artifact identified in step 1(c).
- importGenerationSha256 — over the import generation artifact from step 1(d).

THE SIGNATURE IS THE FENCE. It takes NO caller-supplied digest on any path — a value that cannot be named cannot be echoed. Artifact BYTES arrive through injected read ports so the module stays testable without a second code path; the DIGEST is always computed here, never accepted. A request that spells a digest field is REFUSED with an exact code at this module's own layer, published as a closed TYPE with the layer constant module-private (a column-zero exported `*_LAYER` is a declared production boundary and drags the security roster's BEFORE/AFTER/RACE trio into scope).

ABSENCE REFUSES, NEVER DEFAULTS (taskRail 1): if an artifact cannot be read, answer a refusal naming WHICH artifact — never a zero digest, never an empty string. Persist through the store's expected-version decision path so an identical re-record is a replay rather than a second row.

NEW apps/daemon/src/cutover/cutover-generation-reader.ts (<=250 lines) plus its `.js` bridge. THE ONE PRODUCTION READER (DoD 4): returns the complete FOUR-value snapshot for a given cutover attempt from durable state.

The four values and where each comes from:
- the three recorded by step 3, read back from durable state.
- backupGenerationDigest — COMPOSED, NOT REBUILT (DoD 3, taskRail 2). Read it through the existing durable recovery surface: apps/daemon/src/recovery/durable-recovery-inventory-reader.ts, whose :179-180 already validates the digest against its basis, with the contract at durable-recovery-inventory-contract.ts:72/:248. Record in the row comment exactly which reader you composed and why it is the right one. A FOURTH notion of backup generation that agrees with the recovery lane today will drift from it tomorrow — the same third-notion hazard this board was already burned by on policy refs.

REFUSE DETERMINISTICALLY WHEN ANY OF THE FOUR IS UNAVAILABLE, naming WHICH fact was missing with its exact code and refusing layer. Forward the recovery reader's OWN code and layer unchanged when it is the one that refused — unrestamped, so which authority answered stays legible. Never substitute a zero digest or an empty string for an absent fact: a zero-filled generation compares equal to another zero-filled one, which would make the marker's drift comparison silently vacuous.

RETURN THE SNAPSHOT IN THE SHAPE THE CONSUMER ALREADY DECLARES, so no adapter is needed: `CutoverActivationGenerations` at cutover-activation-marker.ts:28-33 is exactly `{ backupGenerationDigest, distributionManifestSha256, importGenerationSha256, quiesceRecordSha256 }`, all `string`. Match it. Do NOT edit that file — it is task-b2548479's (taskRail 4).

ROSTER DENOMINATORS (epic rail 7) — its own numbered step, not folded into step 2.

(1) THE FOUR-FACT ROSTER: name it as a frozen immutable constant and assert an EXACT count of 4. `length > 0` is not sufficient — a one-member roster satisfies it, and a silently shrunk roster is a snapshot that stops checking a generation. Assert set-equality in BOTH directions between the roster and the keys the reader actually returns: iterating the roster alone shrinks with it and stays green while a fact vanishes from the snapshot.
(2) THE ABSENCE SWEEP from step 2(5) drives one case per fact. Assert it GENERATED exactly 4 cases — a zero-case sweep passes vacuously — and that each names a DISTINCT missing fact. Four cases that all report the same fact would pass a count check while proving one arm four times.
(3) THE REFUSAL-CODE ROSTER: name the module's closed code set as a constant, assert its exact member count, and assert every code the arms drive is a member. A typo'd expectation otherwise asserts a code no authority mints.
(4) Assert the returned snapshot's key set equals `CutoverActivationGenerations`' four keys exactly, so a shape drift between producer and consumer reds here rather than at the consumer's integration.

CONSUMER EDGE AND THE COMPOSITION RECORD (DoD 3 and DoD 5, Rail 8(B)) — its own step because it is a durable claim, not a gate leg.

(a) NAME THE CONSUMER in a row comment with its id: task-b254847909ca4199a70a3a06173f1cd9 consumes this reader for the v2 activation marker. "Exports the symbols" is not composition, and a reader nothing imports satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist — this board has paid for that repeatedly.
(b) DoD 5 says to PREFER landing one durable call site if it can be done without reaching into that row's scope. MEASURE WHETHER IT CAN: cutover-activation-marker.ts is task-b2548479's UNTRACKED WIP and taskRail 4 puts its marker and daemon service out of scope. If wiring the call site means editing that file, DO NOT — record clause (a) as the discharge and say plainly that the edge is named rather than landed, and why. Choosing the named-consumer discharge honestly is correct here; quietly editing a foreign row's WIP to manufacture an edge is not.
(c) RECORD THE COMPOSITION DECISIONS the rails demand: which recovery reader you composed for backupGenerationDigest and why it is the right one (DoD 3), and that the quiesce digest is taken over `serializeLiveEvidence`'s output rather than a second serialization (taskRail 2). Both are claims a later reader will need to check a drift report against.

GATES, MUTATION DRILLS, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, PATHSPEC COMMIT (DoD 7).

GATES — each FOREGROUND, UNPIPED, ALONE. An exit-0 leg printing no count line executed NOTHING.
L1 `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` — quote the `$ tsc --project tsconfig.json` echo; if sub-second, plant one type error as a positive control, confirm red, remove it, prove removal by SHA256.
L2 focused: `(cd apps/daemon && pnpm exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/cutover/cutover-generation-evidence.test.ts src/cutover/cutover-generation-reader.test.ts)` — quote `Test Files`/`Tests`.
L3 `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`.
L4 `(cd apps/daemon && pnpm exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/runtime-entrypoint.test.ts)` — this row adds FOUR new modules with bridges, and that gate reports `missing`/`unexpected`/`wrongContent` BY NAME. Quote the object; it must be all-empty.
A bare `pnpm test` runs ZERO daemon tests (the root vitest include has no apps/**) and proves nothing here. Repo-wide red path-attributed merge-base vs HEAD, owned-path intersection EMPTY, foreign red disclosed verbatim.

DRILLS, each alone, ONE degree of freedom. ALL SIX OWNED FILES ARE NEW AND UNTRACKED (`??`), where `git diff` is BLIND — empty before, during and after a mutation. SHA256 against a %TEMP% backup suffixed by your worker id is the ONLY valid restore proof, taken in a call SEPARATE from the restore. Windows %TEMP%, never MSYS /tmp.
D1 Accept a caller-supplied digest instead of computing it — step 2(1)'s refusal arm must RED on its exact code.
D2 Substitute a ZERO digest for an absent fact instead of refusing — step 2(6)'s absence arm must RED. Then substitute a DIFFERENT non-zero default and confirm it reds too: an arm that only catches zeros would pass any other fabricated default.
D3 Re-serialize the quiesce record locally instead of composing `serializeLiveEvidence` — step 2(2)'s derived-value arm must RED, proving the digest names bytes the rest of the system can reproduce.
D4 Delete one member of the four-fact roster — step 5's exact-count and both set-equality directions RED with nonzero execution.
A GREEN drill is a FINDING to report, never a pass to bank.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (skill `adversarial-self-review`): can any path return a snapshot with a fabricated or defaulted member; does a refusal ever carry a partial snapshot; is the recovery reader's code and layer forwarded unrestamped; can two concurrent records of the same generation both commit.

COMMIT BY EXPLICIT PER-FILE PATHSPEC — and this one matters more than usual. `apps/daemon/src/cutover/` is ENTIRELY task-b2548479's untracked WIP apart from this row's six files. NEVER commit that directory as a pathspec and never `git add -A`: either would sweep their marker into this row's commit. Name each of the six files individually, message BEFORE the `--`, and confirm with `git show --stat` that the commit contains exactly six paths and none of theirs.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 7 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

Six new files, all under apps/daemon/src/cutover/. The artifacts are read, never rebuilt, which is what keeps the row inside the file cap while touching three different producing lanes.

REJECTED — building a producer in each lane (packaging, import, migration). Three lanes plus a reader plus tests exceeds the ten-file cap and would put this row inside three foreign surfaces. The digests are FUNCTIONS of artifacts that already exist; only the digest and its durable record are missing.

A second serialization that agrees today drifts tomorrow, and the digest would then name bytes nobody else can reproduce — taskRail 2 forbids it and drill D3 proves it.

REJECTED — a fourth notion of backupGenerationDigest. It has 43 tracked hits and a durable surface under apps/daemon/src/recovery/ whose reader already validates the digest against its basis (durable-recovery-inventory-reader.ts:179-180). DoD 3 requires composing it; a fourth notion is the third-notion hazard this board already paid for on policy refs.

REJECTED — landing the durable call site into cutover-activation-marker.ts. DoD 5 prefers a call site, but that file is task-b2548479's untracked WIP and taskRail 4 puts its marker out of scope. Step 6 measures whether an edge can be landed WITHOUT reaching into that row and, if not, takes the named-consumer discharge explicitly rather than quietly editing a foreign row's WIP to manufacture one.

REJECTED — defaulting an absent generation to a zero digest or empty string. A zero-filled generation compares EQUAL to another zero-filled one, making the marker's drift comparison silently vacuous. D2 drills both a zero and a non-zero default, because an arm that only catches zeros passes any other fabricated value.
